title: DOC: Fix dtype mismatch in cython example and fix casting example snippet in User Guide to match the text
body: ### PR Summary This PR does two things 1) fixes dtype mismatch in `c-info.python-as-glue.rst` Currently, in the cython zadd function snippet, ```python cdef double complex[:] a = in1.ravel() cdef double complex[:] b = in2.ravel() out = np.empty(a.shape[0], np.complex64) cdef double complex[:] c = out.ravel() ``` the `out` dtype is `np.complex64`. However, the very nextline slices `double complex` which is `np.complex128` . This, when compiled and run, gives following `ValueError`. Fix : Simply change `out` dtype to `np.complex128` to match it. This works fine and adds two complex numbers. (Here, `main.py` imports `zadd` function from compiled cython file, and adds two complex128). 2) improves an example snippet in `basics.types.rst` It says > Sometimes the conversion can overflow, for instance when converting a `numpy.int64` value 300 to `numpy.int8`. NumPy follows C casting rules, so that value would overflow and become 44 ``(300 - 256)``. If you wish to avoid such overflows, you can specify that the overflow action fail by using ``same_value`` for the ``casting`` argument (see also :ref:`overflow-errors`):: Currently, the example for type casting, which aimed to demomstrate ValueError when type casting with `casting='same_value'` option, shows ``` >>> z.astype(np.float64, casting="same_value") array([0., 1., 2.]) ``` Here z is array `[0, 1, 2]`. This example failed to emphasize the said actual behaviour Hence, it can be replaced with following example ``` >>> w = np.array([126,127,128],dtype=np.int64) >>> w.astype(np.int8, casting='same_value') Traceback (most recent call last): File "", line 1, in ValueError: could not cast 'same_value' long to byte ``` I ran `spin docs` and verified both the changes in built html document. #### AI Disclosure Claude Code assisted me in finding these bugs.
